response.title: Can I mount regular rigid solar panels on my shed roof and run them to a portable power station inside?
response.answer:
Yes! You can absolutely mount regular rigid solar panels on your shed roof and connect them to a portable power station inside the shed.

In fact, this is often a better long-term setup than using portable or flexible solar panels because rigid panels are generally more durable, cost-effective, and efficient.

You don't necessarily need a separate solar charge controller, inverter, or battery because a compatible portable power station already has those components built in.

How the setup works
Simplified off-grid shed solar setup (not a complete electrical wiring diagram).

The basic arrangement is:

Rigid solar panels are mounted to the shed roof using proper rails and brackets.

Solar extension cables run from the panels through a weatherproof roof or wall entry.

The cables connect to the power station's solar DC input, often using MC4-compatible connectors and an adapter.

The power station charges its internal battery and powers your devices through its AC outlets, USB ports, or DC outputs.

You can disconnect the power station and take it elsewhere when needed.

Four important things to check

1. Solar input compatibility

This is the most important part. Check your power station's:

Maximum solar input wattage (W)

Solar input voltage range (V)

Maximum input current (A)

Connector type (XT60, XT60i, DC8020, etc.)

For example, a 400W rigid panel might work perfectly with one power station but exceed another's voltage limit. The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc), including its increase in cold weather, must remain below the station's maximum. 
Bluetti Power
+1

2. Roof mounting

Use mounting hardware designed for your roof material, attach it to adequate structural supports, and waterproof all penetrations. Verify that the shed can withstand the panel weight and local wind loads.

3. Cable routing and electrical protection

Use properly rated outdoor PV cables and a weatherproof cable entry. A permanent roof-mounted installation may require grounding, overcurrent protection, disconnects, and permits depending on the configuration and local rules. Have a qualified solar installer or electrician verify these requirements.

4. Temperature inside the shed

This is particularly important in hot climates. Portable power stations have operating-temperature limits, and an unventilated shed can get extremely hot in summer. Keep the unit dry, ventilated, and within its manufacturer's temperature limits.

Example system sizes

Solar panels

	

Power station battery

	

Suitable uses




200W

	

500Wh

	

Lights, phone charging, small electronics




400W

	

1,000Wh

	

Lights, fans, laptop, occasional tools




800W

	

2,000Wh

	

Workshop equipment, larger daily loads

These are illustrative combinations, not guaranteed compatible configurations. Actual performance depends on sunlight, shade, electrical losses, and appliance consumption.

Two questions

Which portable power station do you have (or plan to buy)? For example, EcoFlow DELTA 2, BLUETTI AC180, Jackery Explorer 1000, etc.

What kind of shed roof do you have? Metal, asphalt shingles, or another material?

With those two details, I can help you determine exactly which rigid panels will work, how many you can connect, and the best way to run the cables inside safely.
